## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-*juǎn* anthology of [袾宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%BE%E5%AE%8F) **Yúnqī Zhūhóng**'s Pure Land sayings (*jìngtǔ yǔ* 淨土語) collated from across Yúnqī's prose corpus by his lay-Buddhist disciples [虞執西](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%99%9E%E5%9F%B7%E8%A5%BF) **Yú Zhíxī** and [嚴培西](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9A%B4%E5%9F%B9%E8%A5%BF) **Yán Péixī** in the early seventeenth century, shortly after Yúnqī's death in 1615.

**Abstract**

Yúnqī's Pure Land writings are scattered across many works — the *Ēmítuó jīng shūchāo* [KR6p0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0028), the *Jìngtǔ yíbiàn* [KR6p0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0058), the *Dá sìshíbā wèn* [KR6p0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0063), the *Xīfāng yuànwén* [KR6p0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0064), plus prefaces, letters, and miscellaneous prose pieces preserved in his collected works the *Yúnqī fǎhuì* 雲棲法彙. The *Huìyǔ* extracts and re-organises Yúnqī's most pointed and pastoral Pure Land sayings into a single accessible volume, organised thematically rather than by source-text: opening sections on the doctrinal foundations of Pure Land devotion; sections on practical *niànfó* practice; sections on the deathbed *zhìniàn*; sections of pastoral counsel directed to lay-Buddhist householders and women; sections of polemical responses to Chán objections.

The work belongs to the **post-mortem consolidation of Yúnqī's intellectual legacy** carried out by his lay-Buddhist circle in the decades after his death. Together with the collected *Yúnqī fǎhuì*, the *Wǎngshēng jí*, and the various individual Pure Land writings, the *Huìyǔ* establishes Yúnqī as the **doctrinal centre of late-Míng Pure Land Buddhism** — a status that the subsequent Qīng-period Pure Land masters (Xǐng'ān Shíxián [實賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E8%B3%A2), Hóngluó Dámò [達默](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E9%BB%98), etc.) consistently reinforced.

The text is preserved in the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏 (X1170). No preface fixes a precise composition date; the bracket adopted (1620–1660) covers the early to mid seventeenth century during which the Yúnqī lay-Buddhist circle was consolidating his legacy.
